questions.stem: This intraoperative photograph shows a stenotic congenital pulmonary valve between the right ventricle and the pulmonary artery. What auscultatory finding would you expect in this infant?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Crescendo-decrescendo systolic ejection murmur at the left upper sternal border

choices.label: C
choices.text: Mid-diastolic rumble with an opening snap

explanation.summary: Pulmonary valve stenosis produces a systolic ejection (crescendo-decrescendo) murmur best heard at the left second intercostal space, often with an ejection click.
explanation.whyCorrect: Pulmonary valve stenosis produces a systolic ejection (crescendo-decrescendo) murmur best heard at the left second intercostal space, often with an ejection click.

questions.stem: This netlike, violaceous mottling of the skin developed in a patient following an arterial catheterization procedure. What is this cutaneous finding?

explanation.summary: Livedo reticularis/racemosa is a classic cutaneous sign of cholesterol (atheroembolic) embolization, reflecting occlusion of small dermal arterioles by cholesterol crystals.
explanation.whyCorrect: Livedo reticularis/racemosa is a classic cutaneous sign of cholesterol (atheroembolic) embolization, reflecting occlusion of small dermal arterioles by cholesterol crystals.

questions.stem: These renal biopsies from a hypertensive patient show arteriolar wall changes (arrows). In panel B, the arteriole shows concentric, laminated 'onion-skin' thickening of the wall. This finding is characteristic of what?

explanation.summary: Concentric laminated 'onion-skin' thickening of the arteriolar wall from smooth-muscle hyperplasia is hyperplastic arteriolosclerosis, seen in malignant/accelerated hypertension. It contrasts with the homogeneous pink hyaline thickening (hyaline arteriolosclerosis) of chronic benign hypertension and diabetes.
explanation.whyCorrect: Concentric laminated 'onion-skin' thickening of the arteriolar wall from smooth-muscle hyperplasia is hyperplastic arteriolosclerosis, seen in malignant/accelerated hypertension. questions.stem: This gross lung specimen shows a coarsely nodular, cobblestoned pleural surface with a firm, contracted texture. This appearance is most characteristic of what process?

explanation.summary: The cobblestoned, bumpy pleural surface reflects subpleural fibrosis and honeycomb cystic remodeling of end-stage interstitial lung disease such as idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis. The lung is stiff and contracted rather than hyperinflated (emphysema) or consolidated (pneumonia).
explanation.whyCorrect: The cobblestoned, bumpy pleural surface reflects subpleural fibrosis and honeycomb cystic remodeling of end-stage interstitial lung disease such as idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis. The lung is stiff and contracted rather than hyperinflated (emphysema) or consolidated (pneumonia).
